source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a standardized cultural profile to predict preferences instead of asking the individual client about values or practices.","B":"Exclude cultural practices from the plan whenever biomedical treatment is available, even when the practices are safe.","C":"Avoid discussing culture or health beliefs so cultural differences cannot influence communication or care planning.","D":"Ask about the individual client’s cultural values and practices and incorporate relevant preferences when compatible with safe, effective care."}}
source_row.rationale: HHS CLAS standards call for respectful care responsive to cultural health beliefs and practices; the NCSBN Psychosocial Integrity blueprint specifically includes incorporating client cultural practices and beliefs when planning and providing care.
source_row.source_detail: Principal Standard 1 — care responsive to cultural health beliefs and practices, languages, health literacy and communication needs. National CLAS Standards currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10: cultural practices/beliefs, grief/loss, therapeutic communication and mental-health issues. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: HHS Office of Minority Health — National CLAS Standards
source_row.stem: A nurse plans care for a client whose cultural background differs from the nurse’s. Which action best reflects culturally responsive nursing care?
